chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the woman who gives birth from adultery, and no one knows of that except her guardian: Is it permissible for him to marry her off and remain silent about it, provided he has seen repentance or a good deed from her? He (peace be upon him) said: If he does not mention that to her husband, and then the husband learns of it afterwards, and wishes to take her dower from her guardian for what he concealed from him, then he has that right against her guardian. And the dower which she took for herself, the husband has no claim upon her regarding it, due to what she permitted of her private part. And if her husband wishes to keep her, there is no problem.
ai.seo_question: What are the marital rights and financial compensations when a wife conceals adultery from her husband?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding a woman who conceals prior adultery resulting in childbirth, establishing that the husband may claim the dower from her guardian as compensation for the deception. Crucially, the Imam clarifies that while the husband has the right to annul the marriage or keep her, choosing to retain her means he forfeits the right to reclaim the dower, illustrating the Shia legal principle of 'ikhtiyar' (choice) in marital continuity. This highlights the distinction between the financial penalty for deception and the personal right to maintain the marital bond.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said about the woman who gave birth from the adultery, and no one knew about that except for her guardian. Is it correct for him that he gets her married and maintains silence upon that when he has seen the repentance from her, or she is known for it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he does not mentioned that to her husband, then he comes to know after that, so if he so desires to, he takes her dower from her guardian with whatever was cheated upon him, that being for him upon her guardian (to pay), and the dower which was taken for her, he would not have a way upon her with regards to it due to what she had permitted from her private parts; and if he so desires to he can marry her and keep her, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who gives birth because of going to bed with a man out of wedlock and no one except her guardian knows it, if it is proper for him to give her in marriage and remain quiet about it, provided, he has seen her repenting or good deeds. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he does not mention it to her husband and later he (the husband) comes to know it, if he wants to demand her mahr (dower) from her guardian who cheated, he can do so and the mahr (dower) that he had received, he cannot collect it back from her because of marriage and if her husband wants to keep her it is not unlawful.”’
